meta.description_home: 2,200 km on foot from Switzerland to Santiago to change the way we see: what looks like a lack of willpower is often a misunderstood brain, and it can rebuild itself. Support the cause.

hero.tagline:
Atypical brain, compensating behaviors, rebuilding, it's all connected.
2,200 km to prove it.
hero.subtitle: Roland Crettaz is walking 2,200 km from St-Maurice to Santiago to show in real time that the brain can rebuild itself, and that what looks like weakness of character often hides a misunderstood way the brain works.
hero.h1: It's never a lack of willpower.
hero.intro: Roland Crettaz has been through addiction, collapse and rebuilding. Today he walks to show that recovery is possible, at any age, despite everything.
hero.sub: It's a misunderstood brain, and it can rebuild itself. 2,200 km on foot, from Switzerland to Santiago, to prove it.

projet.title: A physical, neurological and human challenge
projet.subtitle: Three dimensions of the same journey: pushing the body's limits, demonstrating brain plasticity, and sharing a message of hope.
projet.card1_text: 2,200 km on foot, alone, from the Swiss Valais to the Galician coast. Crossing three countries, from the Alps to the Pyrenees, all the way to the Atlantic. An extraordinary human adventure.
projet.card2_text: Neuroplasticity shows that the brain reconfigures itself throughout life. Intensive walking generates BDNF, a protein that promotes neural growth. This pilgrimage is a living neuroscience experiment.
projet.card3_text: ADHD, alcohol, medication, tobacco: Roland Crettaz has been through it all. Today he walks to say that rebuilding is possible, at any age, against all odds.

dimensions.title: Physical, Neurological & Human
dimensions.subtitle: Three dimensions of the same journey: pushing the body's limits, demonstrating brain plasticity, and sharing a message of hope.
dimensions.intro_italic: By covering these 2,200 km, Roland is not only testing his endurance, he is exploring the capacity of the nervous system to reorganise under prolonged effort, turning walking into a genuine open-air clinical study.
dimensions.card_physique_text: Beyond the distance, it is the management of metabolic recovery over more than 80 days of walking that is at stake. Each stage is a lesson in the adaptability of the human body.
dimensions.card_neuro_text: Repetitive bipedal movement promotes a state of "flow". Studies show that long-distance walking stimulates neurogenesis and strengthens connectivity between hemispheres, a powerful emotional regulator for an ADHD brain.
dimensions.card_humain_text: The transition from individual effort to collective resonance. Roland's message becomes a driving force for those who follow him, proving that willpower can reshape biology, and hope, be shared.

roland.title: Roland Crettaz
roland.subtitle: Born in Valais, Roland spent decades with undiagnosed ADHD, trying to fill the void through alcohol, medication and cigarettes.
roland.bio1: It was not until the age of 40 that everything clicked: the ADHD diagnosis, the decision to stop substances, the long road to reconstruction. Therapy, reading, encounters, and then the crazy idea of a 2,200 km walk.
roland.bio2: "The Camino de Compostela is not an escape. It is a return to myself. Every step is a neuron reconnecting, every stage an addiction left behind."
roland.bio3: Roland documents every step: YouTube videos, blog, and a book in preparation. His goal: to become a speaker to address businesses and mental health institutions.
roland.photo_quote: "Every step is therapy. The road gave me back to myself."
roland.story_assoc: This project has given rise to a real structure: the Neuro-Odyssey Association, non-profit, based in Martigny (Valais). Its mission: to raise awareness and support people living with atypical neurological functioning and its consequences. The walk is only the first act.
roland.story_1: More than twenty years ago, alcohol was part of my daily life. Too much. So I stopped, not because it was easy, but because carrying on cost more than changing. Then medication took its place. I stopped again. Years later, tobacco.
roland.story_2: But addiction was only part of the story. There were the money problems. The divorce. The moments when everything wavers inside while you pretend to be fine.
roland.story_3: Instead of running away, I started to observe. To understand why we fall, why we repeat, why we know yet can't do otherwise. I trained, in nutrition, in neuroscience. And along the way, I discovered that I live with ADHD. Not a diagnosis that confines: a key that opens.
roland.story_5b: The road to Compostela is not just a challenge. It's a symbol: of rebuilding, of proof that after falling, you can move forward. Step by step.
roland.story_5c: Supporting this project isn't supporting a man who walks. It's supporting a message: nothing is fixed, you can rise again, and understanding how you work can change a life. This path is mine. But the message is universal.
roland.story_key: It's never a lack of willpower. It's how the whole system works.

docu.title: A Documentary, A Book
docu.subtitle: The journey will be documented in real time. A work that tells the story of reconstruction, not just the walk.
docu.docu_text: Camera on his shoulder, Roland films his daily life as a walker: mountain dawns, conversations with fellow pilgrims, moments of doubt and grace. A film about healing through movement.
docu.book_text: A story of inner as much as outer journey. Blending accessible neuroscience with personal testimony, it speaks to anyone looking to rebuild themselves.
docu.book_title_real: Journey to the Heart of Resilience
docu.book_text_real: A powerful guide to bouncing back, rediscovering inner clarity and moving forward with greater purpose and strength.

preparation.hero_subtitle_prefix: 6 months of intensive preparation for 2,200 km. Here is how Roland prepares his body and mind for the greatest challenge of his life.
preparation.week1_text: Daily outings of 10–15 km. Achilles tendon rehabilitation. First assessment with the physiotherapist.
preparation.week3_text: First long outings of 25 km. Introduction of elevation. Equipment adjustment (Salomon shoes).
preparation.week5_text: Outings of 30–40 km. Consecutive weekends. Test of the 12 kg pack. First night in a mountain hut.
preparation.week9_text: Simulations of Compostela days (25 km/day, 6 consecutive days). Nutritional adjustments.
preparation.pillar_physique_text: Progressive 14-week programme: from 10 km to 40 km per day. Elevation work in the Valais mountains. Bivouac outings to acclimatise the body to real conditions.
preparation.pillar_mental_text: Daily meditation, journaling, work with a sports psychologist. Stress and solitude management protocols for long solo stages.
preparation.pillar_nutrition_text: Adapting diet to the specific needs of the ADHD brain under prolonged effort. Managing dopamine and attention fluctuations over 90 days.
preparation.pillar_equip_text: Testing and selecting every piece of equipment in the field. Partnerships with specialist brands. Target: maximum 9 kg pack.
preparation.nutrition_tagline: What we eat directly impacts brain chemistry, and for an ADHD brain, this is even more true.
preparation.nutrition_p1: The ADHD brain is particularly sensitive to blood sugar fluctuations. Over 90 days of intensive walking, maintaining stable nutritional intake is crucial for emotional regulation and concentration.
preparation.nutrition_p2: Roland worked with a specialist nutritionist to design an adapted protocol: omega-3-rich meals, protein at every stage, anti-crash snacks for long descents.
preparation.nutrition_p3: The goal is not pure athletic performance, it is cognitive consistency over time. A well-nourished brain walks better, thinks more clearly, handles difficult days better.
preparation.nutrition_cta_text: Interested in this nutritional protocol? Roland discusses it in his journal.
preparation.cta_subtitle: Subscribe to the journal to follow each training week, equipment tests and Roland's reflections.

lien.label: Understand
lien.title: Why it's all connected
lien.p1: The atypical brain (an ADHD way of working) naturally tries to make up for a lack of stimulation and emotional regulation. It isn't a lack of willpower. It's neurology.
lien.p2: Alcohol, medication, tobacco, overactivity, excessive risk-taking: these are responses to that lack. They are the brain's attempts to self-regulate with the tools it has on hand.
lien.p3: Once you understand that, everything changes. You stop fighting against yourself. You start understanding yourself.
lien.p4: That's the message Roland is carrying across these 2,200 km.

cause.meta_title: The Cause, Why it's all connected
cause.title: Why it's all connected
cause.subtitle: What no one ever taught us about how the human brain works
cause.s1_title: The starting point: a brain searching for balance
cause.s1_p1: The human brain has one fundamental need: to feel regulated. In balance. Neither over-stimulated nor under-stimulated.
cause.s1_p2: In some people, this regulation system works differently. The brain struggles to maintain that balance on its own. It gets bored quickly, it races, it has trouble filtering information, staying organized, and moving from one emotion to the next without spilling over.
cause.s1_p3: This isn't a character flaw. It isn't laziness or a lack of willpower.
cause.s1_p4: It's a way the brain works. And it's far more common than people think.
cause.s2_title: What the brain does when it can't find balance
cause.s2_p1: When the brain can't find its balance naturally, it looks for shortcuts.
cause.s2_p2: Alcohol slows down what's overflowing. Unprescribed medication numbs what hurts. Cigarettes give the stream of thoughts a tiny pause. Overactivity, risk-taking, screens, food: all of them are ways for the brain to regulate itself with whatever tools it finds.
cause.s2_p3: These behaviors aren't weaknesses. They're imperfect solutions to a real neurological problem.
cause.s2_p4: The trouble is that these solutions create their own dependency, and you end up fighting against your own attempts to survive.
cause.s3_p1: For decades, the symptoms were treated separately.
cause.s3_p2: Alcohol use was treated without looking at what was driving it. Medication was prescribed without understanding why the person kept seeking more. Impulsive behaviors were judged without seeing the brain behind them.
cause.s3_p3: What neuroscience shows today is that, in many cases, it all comes from the same place: a brain that works differently, that was never given the right tools to regulate itself, and that did its best with what it had.
cause.s3_p4: Understanding that means you stop fighting yourself. It's the beginning of rebuilding.
cause.s4_title: What the walk sets out to prove
cause.s4_p1: Long-distance walking isn't a symbol chosen at random.
cause.s4_p2: Neuroscience studies show that regular, sustained physical effort promotes neurogenesis, the brain's ability to create new connections. Walking stimulates the production of proteins that support neuronal growth. It regulates the nervous system. It brings the body and brain back into a state of coherence.
cause.s4_p3: By walking 2,200 km, Roland isn't just crossing three countries. He's experiencing on himself what science describes: that the brain can reconfigure itself, at any age, after any fall.
cause.s4_p4: And he's documenting it in real time, so that this path isn't only his own.
cause.s5_p1: This project is the starting point of a wider vision.
cause.s5_p2: Too many people go through years of confusion, shame, and repeated failures without ever understanding why their brain works the way it does. Too many families search for answers without finding language that is accessible and kind.
cause.s5_p3: A structure dedicated to this awareness is in the works. It will draw on the documentary, the book, and the encounters made along the way to create concrete resources, workshops, content, support, for the people concerned and those close to them.
cause.s5_p4: The walk is its first act. Supporting the Neuro-Odyssée Association means supporting what comes next.

asso.title: The Neuro-Odyssey Association
asso.subtitle: From one man's journey to a project for everyone.
asso.s1_title: From a personal project to a collective cause
asso.s1_p1: The Neuro-Odyssey was born from one man's journey. But the message it carries goes far beyond an individual story.
asso.s1_p2: For this message to live on beyond the walk, it needed a lasting, transparent and independent structure. That is why the Neuro-Odyssey Association was created.
asso.s1_p3: An association isn't just a name. It's a commitment: to keep helping those who need it, long after the 2,200 km.
asso.s2_p1: Raising awareness and supporting people who live with atypical neurological functioning and its consequences, ADHD, burnout, mental overload, addictions, and showing that rebuilding is possible at any age.
asso.s2_p2: Supporting the people concerned and their loved ones with accessible, non-judgemental language, grounded in neuroscience and lived experience.
asso.s2_p3: Showing that you don't rebuild yourself by fighting against yourself, but by understanding how you work.
asso.s3_p1: The association will draw on the documentary, the book and the encounters made along the way to create concrete resources.
asso.s3_p2: Workshops, educational content, testimonies, support: tools for the people concerned as well as for families, caregivers and companies.
asso.s3_p3: The walk is the first act. The rest is built step by step.
asso.s4_p1: The Neuro-Odyssey Association is a non-profit association, with its registered office in Martigny, Valais.
asso.s4_p2: Every donation goes directly to the project: documenting the adventure in real time, creating the resources, and supporting the people concerned.
asso.s4_p3: Supporting the association means making possible what comes after the walk.

mission.outro: The walk begins on August 21, 2026. The countdown starts now.
mission.p1: Too many people living with ADHD, addiction or burnout are told they lack willpower. It's not true, and that belief is what traps them.
mission.p2: The Neuro-Odyssée association exists to spread the word: what we take for a character flaw is often a brain trying to regulate itself. And a brain can be understood, and rebuilt.
mission.reframe: Every sponsored kilometre turns a conviction into proof: you can get back up, and you don't move forward alone.
